qs.q: When examining the carpal bones during an osteology practical, a student identifies the pisiform. Which muscular tendon attaches directly to this bone?
qs.e: The flexor carpi ulnaris tendon attaches to the pisiform bone, which also gives origin to the abductor digiti minimi. Flexor carpi radialis does not attach to this pisiform landmark.
qs.s: PAT III — Progress Assessment Test (8 November 2019) — Revision Guide: MCQs

qs.q: In a carpal bone osteology practical, a student labels several bones including the pisiform, trapezium, trapezoid, and hamate. Which of the remaining carpal bones completes the full set of eight?
qs.e: The full set of carpal bones includes the scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, pisiform, trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, and hamate. Calcaneus, talus, and cuboid are tarsal bones of the foot.
qs.s: PAT III — Progress Assessment Test (8 November 2019) — Revision Guide: MCQs

qs.q: A student palpates a small carpal bone on the ulnar side of the proximal wrist row. Which muscular tendon directly attaches to this specific bone, the pisiform?
qs.e: The flexor carpi ulnaris tendon attaches to the pisiform bone, which also gives origin to the abductor digiti minimi. The other tendons insert or originate elsewhere in the wrist and hand.
qs.s: PAT III — Progress Assessment Test (8 November 2019) — Revision Guide: MCQs

qs.q: A patient presents with deep tenderness in the anatomical snuffbox after falling on an outstretched hand. Which underlying carpal bone is most likely clinically suspected of being fractured?
qs.e: The anatomical snuffbox overlies the scaphoid bone, making tenderness in this space a classic indicator of a scaphoid fracture. The radial pulse is also found traversing this superficial space.
qs.s: Anatomy Spot Revision — Limb, Spine, Histology & Embryology —: MCQs

qs.q: Which carpal bone is directly identified as bone X in the distal carpal row?
qs.e: The trapezium is identified as bone X in the distal carpal row. The scaphoid and lunate belong to the proximal row.
qs.s: Limb Anatomy Revision — Lower & Upper Limb: MCQs

qs.q: In identifying the carpal bones during an anatomy practical, a student locates the pisiform bone. Within the tendon of which muscle does this sesamoid bone develop?
qs.e: The pisiform bone is a sesamoid bone located directly within the tendon of the flexor carpi ulnaris. Flexor carpi radialis inserts on the base of the second and third metacarpals instead.
qs.s: SDL Revision Mock Marathon — Upper Limb, Histology & Embryology —: MCQs

qs.q: While tracing the carpal bones from proximal to distal and lateral to medial during an osteology practical, a student identifies the triquetrum. Which structure is correctly paired with its sequence in this mnemonic?
qs.e: In the standard anatomical mapping, structure 3 is the triquetrum, structure 4 is the trapezium, structure 5 is the trapezoid, and structure 7 is the hamate. The wrong options misattribute these specific numbered identifications.
qs.s: SDL Revision Mock Marathon — Upper Limb, Histology & Embryology —: MCQs

qs.q: While studying the carpal bones, a medical student focuses on the pisiform. Which of the following statements regarding its muscular attachments is correct?
o: Flexor carpi ulnaris inserts into it, and abductor digiti minimi originates from it
Extensor carpi ulnaris inserts into it, and flexor digitorum profundus originates from it
Palmaris longus inserts into it, and adductor pollicis originates from it
Flexor carpi radialis inserts into it, and abductor pollicis brevis originates from it
qs.e: The pisiform bone acts as a sesamoid bone within the tendon of flexor carpi ulnaris, which inserts into it, while abductor digiti minimi originates from it. Flexor carpi radialis inserts on the base of the second and third metacarpals.
qs.s: SDL Revision Mock Marathon — Upper Limb, Histology & Embryology —: MCQs
